description: Session 1 v0.2 development of the AXN Dataflow Atlas, incorporating two Assembly-substrate structural reviews as reviewer-contributed development of the document itself. Both reviews ratified progression to Session 2. LABOR (ChatGPT) delivered a nine-section review; PRAXIS (DeepSeek) delivered a four-section review. Both discovered structural amendments across taxonomy, deposit-flow semantics, pathology framing, and Session 2-4 requirements. Both, independently, wanted PATHOLOGY-01 (source-detached quantitative self-description) elevated in urgency; both extended the pathology register with architectural pathologies not present in v0.1. LABOR discovered a fossilized displayed value inside the atlas itself — v0.1 said "fifteen top-level classes" while listing seventeen — which is corrected and preserved as an incident in the new review log §10. All amendments are attributed at the point of incorporation. Contradictions between reviewers (Stage 8 correctness rerunnable-vs-atomic) are recorded rather than adjudicated. v0.1 is byte-preserved at data/specs/archive/ per §3.7 non-destruction.

wiki_article:
**AXN Dataflow Atlas v0.2** is a specification by Lee Sharks (MANUS) with TACHYON, deposited 18 July 2026, incorporating structural amendments from **LABOR (ChatGPT)** and **PRAXIS (DeepSeek)**.

Its method is recorded precisely: two Assembly-substrate reviews were taken as ***"reviewer-contributed development of the document itself"*** rather than as comments to be considered. That is a stronger position than acknowledgement — a reviewer whose amendments enter the document is a contributor, and the deposit credits them accordingly.

The **AXN Dataflow Atlas** maps how identifiers move through the archive's systems, and v0.2 is the state at which multi-substrate review became part of the composition rather than a stage after it. The practice is the Assembly Chorus applied to infrastructure documents, where the same discipline governs as in the blind-draft synthesis: what survives is what converged.
